choiceReviews.rationale: Changing to cosine can satisfy the index's metric, but it changes the distance the application is explicitly required to measure. The same action is literally appropriate when cosine is acceptable and the existing index matches Embedding. Arguments > METRIC supports that positive context without treating metrics as interchangeable. Even coincident rankings for specially normalized data would not preserve the immutable requirement to continue measuring Euclidean distance.

The documented kNN fallback allows the Euclidean query to execute without compatible indexing, so this option is not an impossible operation. It is a valid positive choice for a workload content to retain exact scanning. It nevertheless supplies no ANN compatibility prerequisite, which is the question's requested change. Working execution and eligibility to use an ANN index are different requirements in the admitted product reference.

An index on a different vector column does not match a query searching Embedding, even when both use Euclidean distance. Arguments > METRIC explicitly requires both properties, rather than either one. The literal index creation would be useful in a valid context where the query searches that other indexed column with Euclidean distance. Changing the searched column to obtain that context would abandon the present question's target.

Keeping Embedding and Euclidean fixed leaves only an applicable Euclidean index on Embedding as the offered way to meet both documented matching conditions. Its positive context is that completed compatible index state, after legitimate provisioning. The wording does not promise concurrent same-column indexes or make this a complete DDL sequence. The latest optimizer may still select kNN; supplying a necessary compatibility condition is not forcing an execution strategy.
